findings.status: New conditional source-level GPU bounds/indexing finding; device admission, application reachability and runtime outcome remain unproved
findings.condition: A direct PrefixSum::record uses a count whose ceil(count/256) blocks exceed 65,535 and whose folded rectangular grid has more slots than logical blocks. The allocated first scratch level has fewer u32 slots than dispatched workgroups (in particular when capacity equals count). Source recording and all relevant native allocations/dispatches must be accepted for the shader to reach the operation.
findings.observation: grid chooses x = min(blocks, 65,535) and y = ceil(blocks/x), which can schedule padded groups. scan_blocks computes the linear block but only guards individual data accesses with index < count; lane 255 writes sums[block] whenever write_sums is set, without checking block < logical blocks. At count 16,776,961 and scratch capacity equal to count, logical blocks and first-level scratch slots are 65,536, while the grid has 131,070 groups; padded groups therefore address outside that bound. This is mathematical source reasoning, not a shader execution or generated fixture. The dated W3C WGSL draft classifies an executed out-of-bounds access as a dynamic error with multiple permitted outcomes; neither guaranteed corruption nor a particular backend response is asserted.
findings.extreme_count_consequence: With count u32::MAX, logical blocks are 2^24 and grid is 65,535 × 257. A padded group with linear block 2^24 computes block * 256 modulo 2^32 as zero, so its lanes pass index < count for the same low data indices as the real first group; add_offsets has the same indexing structure. These overlapping shader accesses and out-of-bounds scratch accesses are conditional on native acceptance and WGSL execution, not observed behavior. They are consequences of the same missing padded-block guard, not separate defect counts.

nonfindings.claim: Zero count is an invalid scan requiring a new error.
nonfindings.reason: record returns success without dispatch on zero, and scratch intentionally retains at least one native slot. This is a documented empty operation, distinct from the unrelated empty-BVH traversal condition.

nonfindings.claim: Wrapping u32 summation alone is an unintended overflow.
nonfindings.reason: The API expressly documents wrapping values. This does not make workgroup address wrap or out-of-bounds indexing intentional.

nonfindings.claim: ScratchTooSmall or BufferTooSmall requires unstructured error text.
nonfindings.reason: ScanError retains typed count or byte extents, while Gpu wraps the native anyhow cause; record checks nonzero count before recording.

nonfindings.claim: An empty padded GPU lane by itself proves an invalid access.
nonfindings.reason: The shader intentionally substitutes zero for lanes with index >= count inside a real partial block. The issue is a padded workgroup outside the number of allocated block sums, a separate bound.

lenses.assessment: The data/sums/count/pad/write_sums names are native shader parameter identifiers matched by PassParameters. Existing 059 parameter-name owner question applies; no defect from literals alone.

BLOCK=256 and MAX_GROUPS=65535 define dispatch and scratch geometry; 4 bytes per word and write_sums modes are ABI roles. Their cross-product bounds, not a blanket literal replacement, need ownership.
ScanElementCount owns scan-word cardinality and is not an interchangeable triangle/BVH count; BufferByteLength owns byte extent. Preserve the 774 exact owner comparison.
Count and byte types are already used at the host API; native WGSL block and lane identities are projected into u32 at the shader boundary.
Logical elements, block counts, rectangular grid slots and scratch capacity are distinct units. The new condition arises when rectangular slots exceed logical block count.
Widened host byte sizing fits u64 for all u32 counts, while shader linear block×256 can wrap and padded block stores lack a logical bound.
Count, data byte size, scratch capacity, recursion levels and dispatch grid must correspond. Local checks bind count to capacity and input bytes but not padded grid slots to the level size.
All u32 counts including zero are representable; accepted device memory/workgroup limits are separate. The folded-grid condition requires actual allocation and dispatch admission.
Native write_sums is a uniform two-state shader mode and unused buffer is a required binding. Its native ABI is distinct from an application policy enum.
Capacity and levels are private and created together, with checked grow replacement. Clone/native buffer concurrency and external data identity remain separate lifecycle questions.
Preserve documented wrapping sums, zero no-op, recursive dispatch order, workgroup barrier uniformity and native ScanError causes in any future change.

Typed count becomes typed byte length before input check, then native count/parameters drive shader workgroups. 774 owner81 rejects reusing this count merely because a BVH or mesh count also uses u32.
ScanElementCount already derives ordinary traits, while ScanError uses thiserror for cause preservation. No bespoke handwritten trait issue is established in this bounded role.
